subject: Recap + next steps: FieldEncounter trial & integration checklist
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya@fieldencounter.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@fieldencounter.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-12-05T11:18:00-08:00
Subject: Recap + next steps: FieldEncounter trial & integration checklist

Hi Maya / Jordan —

Thanks again for a productive call this morning. Quick written recap and proposed next steps so we have shared alignment before the technical kickoff: 

1) Goal / success criteria (trial):
- Integrate Redwood generation endpoint into FieldEncounter’s ticket summarization flow for a 2-week evaluation.
- Success metric: automated summaries match or exceed current heuristic baseline on F1/ROUGE-type measure and reduce average agent resolution time by >= 15% in the sandbox dataset.
- Qualitative gate: CS/ops signoff on hallucination rate for high-priority tickets (< 3% critical hallucinations).

2) Evaluation plan & timeline:
- Week 0 (this week): exchange sandbox sample + test credentials (see asks below).
- Week 1: integration work (SDK + streaming for long context cases), basic A/B on 10k tickets.
- Week 2: iterate prompts/quantization profile, run automated scoring and brief review.
- End of Week 2: short readout + next-step decision (extend, scale, or rollback).

3) Technical scope (what we’ll ship for the trial):
- SDK integration for generation + conversation memory (Node and Python examples attached).
- Streaming responses for ticket-level long context (WebSocket or SSE).
- Tool-calling stub to pull structured customer metadata (will be a simple webhook invocation; Redwood supports JSON tool call responses).
- Fallback path: lower-cost 8-bit quantized model if latency spikes.

4) Ownership / asks (who does what):
- FieldEncounter engineering: provide sandbox dataset (10–15k anonymized tickets), and a single engineering contact for credentials + CORS/network questions (ACTION: provide contact + sample by EOD 2028-12-07).
- Redwood: Neha will own SDK handoff and prompt templates; Ben will own streaming/websocket setup and test harness. I’ll own success criteria tracking and the trial readout.

5) Security & auth notes:
- We recommend ephemeral API tokens scoped to the trial project. We can generate project-scoped tokens and a short-lived signing key for streaming.
- Please confirm if FieldEncounter requires an IP allowlist or VPC peering for this sandbox.

Attachments: fieldencounter_mvp_requirements.xlsx (sample schema), redwood_sdk_integration_guide.pdf (node/python examples + streaming section).

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Maya/Jordan: confirm dataset ETA and engineering contact.
- Neha/Ben: initial internal sync today to align on SDK examples and streaming test harness (I’ll schedule).
- Team: target kickoff session next week once credentials are in place.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this running.

Best,
Priyom
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks Priyom — this is very clear. A few clarifications from our side before we hand off to eng: 

- Dataset: we can provide a 12k anonymized ticket dump (JSONL) by tomorrow (2028-12-06 EOD PT). Good?
- Streaming vs polling: for long customer threads we prefer streaming (near real-time agent UX). Can you confirm whether Redwood’s streaming is WebSocket-based or SSE? Also: how does session resume/partial transcript work with the KV cache?
- Tool-calling: we will need a synchronous tool call to our metadata service (customer tier, SLA flags). Is the Redwood tool-calling model synchronous out of the box or should we implement an intermediary webhook?

One more point — we need basic performance numbers for the chosen model (p50/p95 latency for a 1k-token context). If you can attach an expectation number or a short benchmark we can use for acceptance, that would help.

Once we have that, I’ll loop in our lead engineer (Asha) and schedule the kickoff.

—Jordan
Jordan Lee
Head of Product Engineering
FieldEncounter

Jordan — good questions. Answers and action assignments below.

1) Streaming protocol & KV cache
- Redwood supports both WebSocket-based streaming and Server-Sent Events (SSE). For bi-directional low-latency UX we recommend WebSocket.
- Session resume: KV cache is keyed by session_id; during resume the client replays the last N KV entries (configurable) — the SDK examples attached show a resume flow where the client sends resume_token and the server returns missing KV frames.

2) Tool-calling
- Redwood offers a JSON tool-calling contract; the model will emit a JSON payload that our runtime can either (a) call your webhook synchronously and return the result into the generation flow, or (b) emit the tool-call as a structured output for your service to poll. For low-latency metadata (customer tier lookup) we recommend the synchronous webhook path. Ben will produce an example webhook signature.

3) Perf expectations (sandbox)
- Ballpark numbers for the initial model variant (medium-size contextual): p50 ~ 180–240 ms per 1-token step for 1k-token prompts on a dedicated GPU in our hosted environment; end-to-end for a 200-token generation typically falls in the 350–500 ms range depending on decoding. We’ll provide targeted p50/p95 once we run the sample through our quick-benchmark.

4) Owners & immediate tasks (short checklist)
- FieldEncounter: provide 12k JSONL sample + add Asha as eng contact (ACTION: Maya/Jordan — by 2028-12-06 EOD).
- Redwood: Neha to share Node/Python SDK snippets and prompt templates (ATTACHMENT: redwood_sdk_integration_guide.pdf). Ben to share streaming test harness and webhook signature example. Priyom to set up trial project and ephemeral tokens. (ETA internal: 24–48 hours).

5) Proposed kickoff slot
- We can do Thursday 2028-12-07 or Tuesday 2028-12-12 for a 60-minute kickoff focused on hands-on integration. Please propose which works for your eng team.

I’m attaching the SDK guide and an initial requirements worksheet. I’ll schedule an internal sync with Neha/Ben now.

Best,
Priyom
